header.name: Machine Learning Techniques for Real-time Control
header.description: This course will provide an in-depth understanding of how to apply machine learning (ML) tools for real-time control applications, where no a-priopri data is available for the training phase of the ML component. The course focuses on online applications like control of robotics, aircraft type plants, which can be modelled as nonlinear dynamical systems. The uncertainties associated with the plant dynamics would be learned online using ML components (like neural networks), while simultaneously ensuring stability of the plant. Further model-based reinforcement learning (RL) inspired techniques will be introduced to design an approximate optimal controller. Lyapunov-based stability analysis will be instrumental for designing all the mentioned controllers.
prerequisites_mandatory: No pre-requisite as such. A basic familiarity with concepts of Linear Systems, Linear Algebra

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the fundamentals of nonlinear dynamical systems and control, familiarize with basic tools for stability analysis and controller design

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the principles of adaptive control design

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Extend the philosophy of adaptive control to ML-based real-time control with various robust modifications

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Understand RL-inspired Control design principles, which ensure approximate optimality

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze the controllers while ensuring stability, convergence, optimality and performance bounds

lecture_topics: Introduction to Nonlinear Dynamical Systems and Control
Adaptive Control techniques for structured uncertainty
Machine Learning based real-time control design for unstructured uncertainty using various learning mechanisms
introduction to robust modifications like dead-zone
Reinforcement learning-based algorithms for approximate optimal control (AOC) design
policy iteration: on-plicy and off-policy methods for AOC design

resources.title: Neural Network Control of Robot Manipulators and Nonlinear Systems by Lewis, Jagannathan and Yesildirek
Optimal Adaptive Control and Differential Games by Reinforcement Learning Principles by Vrabie, Vamvoudakis and Lewis
Applied Nonlinear Control by Slotine and Li
